mainTopic: The end of רב אסי's discussion of מצה of מעשר שני, and the משנה's rules for an אתרוג of תרומה, דמאי and מעשר שני, and for blemished, tipless and peeled אתרוגים
overview: This amud joins the sugya in the middle. It finishes the source for רב אסי's view that, according to רבי מאיר, מצה of מעשר שני does not fulfill the obligation: a גזירה שוה links מצה to חלה, so both must be 'yours'. The גמרא tries to support this from a ברייתא where רבי מאיר exempts מעשר שני dough from חלה. It then asks whether that dispute really carries over to מצה, since the Torah writes 'עריסותיכם' twice about חלה. The גמרא then returns to the משנה. An אתרוג of impure תרומה is פסול. An אתרוג of pure תרומה is not taken at the start, for one of two reasons given by רבי אמי and רבי אסי, but it is כשר if taken. An אתרוג of דמאי depends on whether a poor person may eat דמאי, which is a מחלוקת of בית שמאי and בית הלל. An אתרוג of מעשר שני in ירושלים follows the same pattern as pure תרומה. Next comes רב's ruling on חזזית, which רבא challenges and the גמרא corrects. The גמרא also explains the missing פיטם. Finally, רבא rules that an אתרוג peeled like a red date is כשר; the משנה is raised against him, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Linking מצה to חלה: it must be yours, not מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The verse about חלה, 'when you eat of the bread of the land', is used to teach that just as חלה applies only to what is 'yours' and not to מעשר שני, so too מצה must be 'yours' and not מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And it shall be, when you eat of the bread of the land.' Just as there (with חלה) it must be from what is yours and not from מעשר, so too here (with מצה) it must be from what is yours and not from מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes building the source for רבי מאיר's view: it compares מצה to חלה. Since חלה applies only to food that is fully 'yours', the same is true of מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both מצה ('לחם עוני', bread of affliction) and חלה ('לחם הארץ', bread of the land) are called 'bread', so the rules of one are carried over to the other through a גזירה שוה. רבי מאיר holds that מעשר שני belongs to Heaven (ממון גבוה), not to you. So dough of מעשר שני is exempt from חלה, and the same 'not yours' status means a person does not fulfill the מצוה with מצה of מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching method that links two topics because they share a word
'Just as there, so too here': the formula that applies the rule of one case to another
Second tithe, which must be eaten in ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: 'Over there' (לְהַלָּן) means חלה, the verse just quoted. 'Here' (כָּאן) means מצה. Do not mix them up: the verse quoted is about חלה, not about מצה.

phrases.english: "And it shall be when you eat of the bread of the land"
Just as there (challah), it must be from yours
and not from tithe,
so too here (matza), it must be from yours
phrases.notes: Here means the מצה eaten on פסח.

phrases.english: and not from tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהַלָּן מִשֶּׁלָּכֶם וְלֹא מִשֶּׁל מַעֲשֵׂר אַף כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation that began on the previous amud (the 'לחם לחם' link for רב אסי's statement)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, מצה, like חלה, must be 'yours', so מצה of מעשר שני does not fulfill the obligation.

steps.title: A suggested support from the dispute about מעשר שני dough and חלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that a ברייתא supports רב אסי: רבי מאיר exempts dough of מעשר שני from חלה, while חכמים obligate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him? 'Dough of מעשר שני is exempt from חלה. These are the words of רבי מאיר. חכמים say: it is obligated in חלה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא and suggests it backs up רב אסי's split between רבי מאיר and חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides of the ברייתא line up exactly with רב אסי's two sides. רבי מאיר holds that מעשר שני is not 'yours', so there is no חלה, and by extension one cannot fulfill the מצה obligation with it. חכמים hold that it is 'yours', so there is חלה, and by extension one fulfills the מצה obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?
The portion of dough given to a כהן

phrases.english: Shall we say that this supports him (Rav Asi):
Dough of second tithe
is exempt from challah,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
It is obligated in challah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for outside support for the ruling just derived
steps.raayaObject: רב אסי's statement that מצה of מעשר שני depends on the dispute between רבי מאיר and חכמים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: רבי מאיר exempts dough of מעשר שני from חלה, and חכמים obligate it

steps.title: Why call it 'support'? It is the very same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to its own wording: the ברייתא is not merely support for רב אסי, it is exactly his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Shall we say it supports him?' It is the very same thing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own suggestion. You cannot call something 'support' when it is the exact source רב אסי built his teaching on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי's statement rests on the גזירה שוה from חלה. That means it depends directly on this dispute about חלה. Calling the ברייתא 'support' makes no sense, because it is simply the same dispute. So the question 'does it support him?' needs to be reworded.

keyTerms.meaning: It is the very same thing

phrases.english: "Shall we say it supports him?"
It is the very same thing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the framing of step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'shall we say it supports him' in step 2
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A source cannot be 'support' for a teaching that is built directly on it. The two are identical.

steps.title: The real question: does the חלה dispute carry over to מצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords its question: since רבי מאיר and חכמים argue about חלה, should we assume they also argue about מצה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is the question: since they argue about this (חלה), do they also argue about that (מצה)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of its question. It is not asking whether the ברייתא supports רב אסי. It is asking whether the חלה dispute automatically extends to מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new question is about whether רב אסי's extension is valid. רבי מאיר clearly exempts מעשר שני dough from חלה. What is uncertain is whether he would also say that מצה of מעשר שני fails for the פסח obligation. If the dispute carries over, רב אסי is confirmed.

phrases.english: Rather: since they argue about this (challah),
do they also argue about that (matza)?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִדִּבְהָא פְּלִיגִי בְּהָא נָמֵי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 3 by rewording the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was offered as plain support for רב אסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The real question is whether the חלה dispute automatically extends to מצה.

steps.title: Perhaps dough is different: 'your dough' appears twice
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the dispute does not carry over. With חלה, the Torah writes 'עריסותיכם' twice, which stresses that the dough must be yours. Matza has no such doubled wording, so even רבי מאיר might allow מצה of מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps dough is different, because the verse says 'your dough', 'your dough', two times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers the other side of the question. The ownership rule may be special to חלה, so no proof for רב אסי can be drawn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doubled word 'עריסותיכם' may be what makes ownership so strict for חלה. Since מצה lacks this doubled wording, רבי מאיר might agree that one fulfills the obligation with מצה of מעשר שני. The question is left open, so the proof for רב אסי is not established.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about חלה does not prove רב אסי's ruling about מצה. Ownership may matter more for חלה because 'עריסותיכם' is written twice.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not reject רב אסי's ruling. It only shows that the ברייתא about חלה cannot prove it, because חלה may have a special extra emphasis on ownership.

phrases.english: Or perhaps: dough is different,
for the verse says
"your dough", "your dough"
two times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the question posed in step 4, which undercuts the proof
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the חלה dispute as proof for the מצה ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חלה has a special doubled word stressing ownership, so its rule may not carry over to מצה

steps.title: Back to the משנה: an אתרוג of impure תרומה is פסול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: an אתרוג of impure תרומה is פסול, because it may not be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One of impure תרומה is פסול.' This is because it has no permission to be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the מצה discussion and returns to the next ruling in the משנה, explaining it briefly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure תרומה is forbidden to eat, even for a כהן. It must be burned. Following the principle discussed earlier, an אתרוג used for the מצוה must be fit to eat, so an inedible אתרוג is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure teruma, which must be burned

steps.whyThisMatters: It applies the rule that an אתרוג for the מצוה must be something that is allowed to be eaten.

phrases.english: "One (an etrog) of impure teruma is invalid."
phrases.notes: This line is quoted from the משנה.

phrases.english: Because it has no permission to be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: returns to the next clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אתרוג of impure תרומה is פסול, because it may not be eaten.

steps.title: Why not take an אתרוג of pure תרומה: two reasons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that one should not take an אתרוג of pure תרומה. רבי אמי and רבי אסי give two different reasons: one says the person makes it able to become impure, the other says he damages it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: an אתרוג of pure תרומה, one should not take it. רבי אמי and רבי אסי disagree about why. One says: because he makes it able to become impure. The other says: because he damages it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about pure תרומה. It brings two different reasons why one should not take such an אתרוג at the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one: a person holding wet הדסים and ערבות touches the אתרוג with wet hands. That makes it able to become impure (הכשר), and we may not cause תרומה to become impure. Reason two: handling the אתרוג spoils its peel, and we may not waste תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure תרומה, the holy portion given to a כהן, which may still be eaten
He makes it able to become impure (by getting it wet)

steps.confusionAlert: 'לא יטול' means 'should not take at the start'. It does not mean the אתרוג is פסול. The משנה will soon say that if he took it, it works.

phrases.english: And one of pure teruma, he should not take.

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi disagree about it,
one said: because he makes it susceptible to impurity,
phrases.notes: Wet hands from the water the other species are kept in make the fruit able to become impure.

phrases.english: and one said: because he damages it.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from impure תרומה (step 6) to pure תרומה in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not take an אתרוג of pure תרומה at the start. The reason is either that it becomes able to become impure, or that it gets damaged.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the two reasons ever lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the next step: when would the two reasons give different answers?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons forbid taking the אתרוג in the ordinary case. So the גמרא wants a case where only one of the reasons applies.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the dispute in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the 'susceptibility' reason and the 'damage' reason lead to different rulings.

steps.title: The case: תרומה declared on everything except the outer peel
steps.stepSummary: Suppose someone declared the אתרוג תרומה except for its outer peel. The 'susceptibility' reason still forbids taking it. The 'damage' reason does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, where he declared it תרומה except for its outer peel. According to the one who says 'because he makes it able to become impure', the problem is there. According to the one who says 'because he damages it', the problem is not there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. It gives a case where only one of the two reasons applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the peel is ordinary, not holy, food, then spoiling the peel does not waste any תרומה. So the 'damage' reason falls away. But wet hands still make the whole fruit, including the holy inside, able to become impure. So the 'susceptibility' reason still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: There is (a problem) / there is not

phrases.english: For example, where he declared it teruma
except for its outer peel.
According to the one who said 'because he makes it susceptible', there is a problem.
According to the one who said 'because he damages it', there is no problem.
phrases.notes: The peel that gets spoiled was never תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן שֶׁקָּרָא עָלֶיהָ שֵׁם חוּץ מִקְּלִיפָּתָהּ חִיצוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the outer peel was left as ordinary food, only the 'susceptibility' reason forbids taking the אתרוג.
steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons for avoiding pure תרומה: making it able to become impure, and wasting it. They differ when the peel itself is not תרומה.

steps.title: Why the תרומה אתרוג still works after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if someone took an אתרוג of pure תרומה, it works. The גמרא explains that both earlier reasons for disqualifying an אתרוג do not apply here: it may be eaten, and it has money value.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And if he took it, it is כשר.' According to the one who says an אתרוג is פסול when it may not be eaten: this one may be eaten. According to the one who says an אתרוג is פסול when it has no money value: this one has money value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה. It shows that this אתרוג passes the test of each of the two earlier opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, two reasons were given for why some אתרוגים are פסול. One reason is that the fruit may not be eaten. The other is that it has no money value, so it does not truly count as 'yours'. Pure תרומה may be eaten by a כהן, and it can be sold to a כהן. So under either opinion the אתרוג is כשר. It is only avoided at the start, for the reasons in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: And if he did take it, it is valid
Money value (it can be owned and sold)

phrases.english: And if he took it, it is valid.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ הֶיתֵּר אֲכִילָה —
phrases.english: According to the one who said it is invalid because it has no permission to be eaten,
this one does have permission to be eaten;

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דִּין מָמוֹן —
phrases.english: according to the one who said it is invalid because it has no monetary value,
this one does have monetary value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's rule about pure תרומה. It ties the rule back to the reasons for פסול discussed earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אתרוג of pure תרומה is כשר after the fact, because it may be eaten and has money value.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the difference between 'should not take at the start' (לכתחילה) and 'פסול'. Only a failure of eating or money value makes the אתרוג פסול.

steps.title: Why do בית הלל allow an אתרוג of דמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about דמאי and asks for the reason of בית הלל, who rule that such an אתרוג is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And an אתרוג of דמאי.' What is the reason of בית הלל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה, דמאי. It sets up the next step by asking why בית הלל say it is כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דמאי is produce bought from someone who may not have separated מעשרות, so ordinarily we may not eat it. That seems like it should make the אתרוג פסול, just like other fruit that may not be eaten. So the גמרא needs to explain why בית הלל allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from someone who may not have separated מעשרות; it is doubtful, so one should not eat it before separating

phrases.english: And one of demai.
What is the reason of Beit Hillel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה, דמאי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why בית הלל allow an אתרוג of דמאי, even though one may not normally eat דמאי.

steps.title: He could make himself poor, so it counts as 'yours'
steps.stepSummary: Anyone could declare all his property ownerless and become a poor person, and a poor person may eat דמאי. So even now the אתרוג counts as 'לכם', 'yours'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since, if he wanted, he could declare all his property ownerless and become poor, and then the דמאי would be fit for him to eat. So even now, we call it 'לכם' ('yours').
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives בית הלל's reason. Because the owner could easily make this fruit permitted for himself to eat, it already counts as fully usable and 'his'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says 'ולקחתם לכם', 'take for yourselves'. A fruit that is forbidden to eat might fail that requirement. But דמאי is permitted to a poor person, and anyone can become poor by declaring his property ownerless (הפקר). Since that option is always available to him, the fruit is treated as usable for him right now.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For yourselves', from 'ולקחתם לכם', the requirement that the four species be yours
We call it / we read the word as applying to it

phrases.english: Since, if he wants,
he can declare his property ownerless,
and he becomes poor, and it is fit for him to eat;
now too, we call it 'for yourselves'.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאִי בָּעֵי מַפְקַר לְהוּ לְנִכְסֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because he could become poor through הפקר, and a poor person may eat דמאי, the אתרוג already counts as 'לכם'.
steps.confusionAlert: He does not actually have to make his property ownerless. The fact that he could is enough to make the אתרוג count as 'yours'.

steps.title: Source: the poor may be fed דמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה as the source that poor people, and soldiers quartered in the town, may be fed דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: we may feed poor people דמאי, and we may feed soldiers quartered in the town דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the claim in step 12, that a poor person may eat דמאי, by quoting a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole reasoning of step 12 depends on the rule that דמאי is permitted to a poor person. This משנה states that rule openly. That completes the explanation of בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Soldiers or troops staying in the town, whose food the residents must provide

phrases.english: As we learned: one may feed the poor demai,
and quartered soldiers demai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule that step 12 relies on.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a poor person may eat דמאי, which is the basis of בית הלל's reasoning.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה: מאכילין את העניים דמאי ואת אכסניא דמאי.
steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל allow an אתרוג of דמאי. Anyone can become poor through הפקר, and the poor may eat דמאי, so the fruit counts as 'לכם'.

steps.title: Why בית שמאי disqualify an אתרוג of דמאי
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי hold that a poor person may not eat דמאי, so the 'become a poor person' trick does not make the אתרוג count as 'yours.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי? They hold that a poor person may not eat דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why בית שמאי disagree with בית הלל, and answers right away: according to them, a poor person may not eat דמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל's reason was that anyone can declare his property ownerless, become a poor person, and then eat דמאי. That makes the אתרוג 'לכם' (yours). בית שמאי reject the starting point: even a poor person may not eat דמאי. So the reasoning never gets off the ground, and the אתרוג is not considered 'yours.'

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai (why do they disqualify it)?
phrases.notes: The גמרא asks this in shorthand, just 'And בית שמאי?', and means: why do they disqualify it?

phrases.english: A poor person may not eat demai

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי, עָנִי לָא אָכֵיל דְּמַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the מחלוקת, after the reason of בית הלל was explained.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the reason of בית שמאי, who disqualify an אתרוג of דמאי?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to them, a poor person may not eat דמאי, so the אתרוג is never 'yours.'

steps.title: The משנה about feeding poor people and soldiers דמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the משנה about whether poor people and quartered soldiers may be fed דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: 'One may (not) feed poor people דמאי, nor soldiers quartered in the town דמאי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for the idea that poor people's eating of דמאי is a debated topic. It is setting up רב הונא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same משנה cited in step 13 for בית הלל, here quoted in the 'not' version. On its own, it does not show who disagrees. The next step, from רב הונא, reveals that this is a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Soldiers quartered in the town, whose food the residents must supply

steps.confusionAlert: The word (אֵין) appears in parentheses in our printed text. The standard text of the משנה permits feeding them דמאי, which is בית הלל's view. The 'not' version is the view of בית שמאי, as the next step shows.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
One may (not) feed the poor demai
and the quartered soldiers demai

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text behind the claim made in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that whether a poor person may eat דמאי is a matter of dispute
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in דמאי about feeding poor people and soldiers

steps.title: רב הונא shows it is a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא cites a ברייתא: בית שמאי forbid feeding poor people and soldiers דמאי, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא said: It was taught in a ברייתא: בית שמאי say one may not feed poor people and soldiers דמאי. בית הלל say one may feed poor people and soldiers דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא brings a ברייתא showing that בית שמאי and בית הלל argue exactly about feeding poor people דמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties everything together. Because בית שמאי forbid a poor person to eat דמאי, the 'make yourself poor' logic fails for them, and the אתרוג of דמאי is פסול. Because בית הלל permit it, the logic works for them, and the אתרוג is כשר.
steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת about an אתרוג of דמאי depends on a broader מחלוקת: may a poor person eat דמאי? בית הלל say yes, so the אתרוג is 'yours' and כשר. בית שמאי say no, so it is פסול.

phrases.english: And Rav Huna said:
It was taught: Beit Shammai say:
One may not feed the poor
or the quartered soldiers demai
And Beit Hillel say:
One may feed the poor demai
and the quartered soldiers demai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה from step 15 as a מחלוקת, which completes the proof for step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי hold a poor person may not eat דמאי

steps.title: An אתרוג of מעשר שני in ירושלים: both reasons apply
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says not to take an אתרוג of מעשר שני in ירושלים in the first place. Both earlier reasons explain why.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה continues: 'Of מעשר שני in ירושלים' (one should not take it). According to the one who says the reason is that he makes it susceptible to impurity, here too he makes it susceptible. According to the one who says the reason is that he damages it, here too he damages it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, an אתרוג of מעשר שני in ירושלים. It shows that both explanations given earlier for pure תרומה also apply here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני must be kept pure, just like תרומה. Handling the אתרוג wet makes it susceptible to impurity. Shaking it during the מצוה also damages its peel, and the peel is food that must not be wasted. So under either reason, one should not take it לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, eaten in purity in ירושלים
He makes it susceptible to impurity

phrases.english: (An etrog) of second tithe in Jerusalem.
According to the one who says it is because he makes it susceptible —
here too he makes it susceptible;
according to the one who says it is because he damages it —
here too he damages it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from דמאי to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אתרוג of מעשר שני in ירושלים should not be taken לכתחילה, under either reason (susceptibility or damage).

steps.title: If he took it, it is כשר, and which תנא this follows
steps.stepSummary: After the fact, an אתרוג of מעשר שני works. Under the 'permitted to eat' reason, everyone agrees. Under the 'monetary value' reason, this follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And if he took it, it is כשר.' According to the one who said (ערלה is פסול) because it may not be eaten, this is everyone's view. According to the one who said it is because it has no monetary status, whose view is this? It is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the משנה's ruling that an אתרוג of מעשר שני works after the fact. It does this using the two reasons given earlier for why an אתרוג of ערלה is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני may be eaten in ירושלים, so under the 'permitted to eat' reason everyone agrees it is כשר. Under the 'monetary value' reason, it depends on a dispute. רבי מאיר holds that מעשר שני belongs to Heaven (ממון גבוה), so it is not 'yours.' The רבנן hold it belongs to the owner. So the משנה here follows the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Status as one's own property (monetary value)

phrases.english: And if he took it — it is fit.
According to the one who said
because it has no permission to be eaten —
this is everyone's view.
According to the one who said
because it has no monetary status —
whose view is this? It is the Rabbis'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same case, now giving the ruling after the fact (בדיעבד).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the fact, an אתרוג of מעשר שני works. Under the 'monetary value' reason, this follows the רבנן against רבי מאיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that each reason given for ערלה produces different results for other cases, so the משנה ends up following specific authorities.

steps.title: רב חסדא quotes רב: blemishes in several places are כשר
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's case of חזזית, רב חסדא reports רב's ruling: it is פסול only if the blemish is in one place, but כשר if spread over two or three places.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If חזזית arose on it' (it is פסול). רב חסדא said: Our great teacher said this, may the Omnipresent help him: This was taught only in one place, but in two or three places it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the משנה's case of boil-like blemishes. רב חסדא, quoting his teacher רב, limits the פסול to blemishes gathered in one spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads the משנה narrowly. Only a blemish concentrated in one place is פסול. If it is spread out in smaller patches over two or three spots, the אתרוג is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Boil-like blemishes or scabs on the peel
They taught this only in the case of

phrases.english: If boil-like blemishes arose (on it).
Rav Chisda said:
This thing our great teacher said,
may the Omnipresent be his help:
They taught this only in one place,
but in two or three places — it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the משנה about physical blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזזית is פסול only if it is in one place. Spread over two or three places, the אתרוג is כשר.

steps.title: רבא: several places makes it spotted and פסול
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues the opposite: blemishes in two or three places make the אתרוג look spotted, so it is certainly פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: On the contrary! In two or three places it is like something spotted, and it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב חסדא's report and flips it. Spread-out blemishes are worse, not better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's logic is about the beauty of the אתרוג (הדר). Patches in several spots make it look spotted, which ruins its appearance even more than a single blemish. So he holds the opposite of רב's ruling.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
On the contrary, in two or three places
it is like something spotted, and is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the ruling in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that blemishes in two or three places are כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Spread-out blemishes make the אתרוג look spotted (מנומר), which damages its beauty more. So it should be פסול, not כשר.

steps.title: רב's ruling moved to the second half of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes where רב's ruling was said. It was said on the משנה's line 'on its minority, it is כשר.' There it adds a stricter rule: one spot is כשר, but two or three spots make the אתרוג look spotted, so it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if this was said, it was said on the second half of the משנה: 'If the blemish is on a minority of it, it is כשר.' רב חסדא said: Our great teacher said this, and may God help him: They only taught this when the blemish is in one place. But in two or three places, it is like a spotted fruit, and it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא's challenge from the last step. It says רב's ruling was actually said on a different line of the משנה, and so it really means the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב made the אתרוג more lenient (spread blemishes = כשר), and רבא showed this makes no sense. Now רב's ruling is attached to the line 'a blemish on a minority is כשר,' and it limits that leniency: a small blemish is כשר only in one spot. If it is spread out, it looks spotted and is פסול, which matches רבא's logic.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said — used to fix the wording or placement of a statement
The later part of a משנה
Its minority — less than half of it
They only taught this when — a phrase that limits a rule

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions use the same words 'one place' versus 'two or three places,' but the result flips. In the corrected version, spread-out spots are פסול, not כשר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the version that stands: small blemishes spread over several spots disqualify the אתרוג, even if together they cover only a small part of it.

phrases.english: Rather: if it was stated
it was stated on the latter clause.
phrases.notes: The second half of the משנה about חזזית.

phrases.english: On its minority — it is fit.
Rav Chisda said:
This matter, our great teacher said it,
and may the Omnipresent be in his help:
they taught this only in one place,
but in two or three places —
it is like a spotted fruit, and it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's objection by moving רב's ruling to a different line of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing which line of the משנה the statement refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב said spread-out blemishes are כשר, which is illogical because they look spotted.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב was limiting the leniency of a minority blemish: it is כשר only in one spot; spread over several spots it is פסול.

steps.title: A blemish on the top of the אתרוג disqualifies at any size
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a blemish on the חוטם (the top, narrow part of the אתרוג) makes it פסול even if it is tiny.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And on its top part, even a tiny amount also makes it פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new rule: the 'minority is כשר' leniency does not apply to the top part of the אתרוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a small blemish in one spot is allowed. But the חוטם is the most visible part and where the אתרוג's beauty shows most. So any blemish there, however small, disqualifies it.

keyTerms.meaning: Its 'nose' — the top part of the אתרוג that narrows toward the tip

steps.whatToRemember: Small blemish in one spot = כשר. Small blemishes spread over several spots = פסול. Any blemish on the חוטם = פסול.

phrases.english: Rava said:
and on its top part —
even with any tiny amount, it is also unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the 'minority is כשר' rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blemish on the חוטם of the אתרוג disqualifies it even if tiny.

steps.title: What 'its פיטם was removed' means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case 'its פיטם was removed,' and a ברייתא of רבי יצחק בן אלעזר explains it as 'its pestle-shaped tip was removed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If its פיטם was removed.' רבי יצחק בן אלעזר taught: If its pestle-like tip was removed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה and explains which part of the אתרוג the word פיטם means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls the פיטם a בוכנא, a 'pestle,' because it sticks out from the top of the אתרוג like the handle of a pestle. This makes clear which part must be missing for the אתרוג to be פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Its פיטם — the small knob at the top of the אתרוג
Its pestle — the pestle-shaped tip at the top

phrases.english: Its pitam was removed.
Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar taught:
Its pestle-like tip was removed.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִטְּלָה פִּטְמָתוֹ. תָּנָא רַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פיטם is the pestle-shaped tip at the top of the אתרוג; if it is removed, the אתרוג is פסול.

steps.title: An אתרוג peeled like a red date is fit
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's case of a peeled אתרוג, רבא rules that if only the thin outer skin came off, like a red date, it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If it was peeled.' רבא said: An אתרוג that was peeled like a red date is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the משנה's case of a peeled אתרוג, and רבא gives a lenient ruling for one kind of peeling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A red date has a very thin skin. רבא means that if only the thin outer layer of the אתרוג came off, the rest of the fruit stays intact, so it is כשר. This looks like it goes against the משנה, which sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: That was peeled / had its skin come off
A red date (a date with a thin red skin)

phrases.english: It was peeled.
Rava said:
This etrog that was peeled
like a red date — is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִקְלַף. אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי אֶתְרוֹגָא דְּאַגְלֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אתרוג whose thin outer skin was peeled like a red date is כשר.

steps.title: Challenge: the משנה says a peeled אתרוג is unfit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: the משנה clearly says a peeled אתרוג is פסול, so how can רבא call it כשר?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: If it was peeled, it is פסול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's ruling using the plain words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives no exception: 'peeled' means פסול. רבא said a peeled אתרוג can be כשר, which seems to go straight against it.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned (in the משנה) — introduces a challenge from a משנה

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
If it was peeled — it is unfit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling from the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that an אתרוג peeled like a red date is כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה states with no exception that a peeled אתרוג is פסול, which contradicts רבא.

steps.title: Start of the answer: it is not difficult
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer: 'This is not difficult.' The actual explanation continues in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: This is only the opening of the answer. The גמרא is getting ready to explain how רבא and the משנה can both be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא קשיא' tells us the גמרא will show that the משנה and רבא are talking about two different cases. The details of the difference come in the next section.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult — opens an answer, usually by showing two different cases

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
phrases.notes: The explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge from the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing two different cases (the details come in the next section)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's ruling seems to contradict the משנה's 'peeled is פסול.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer will show that רבא and the משנה are talking about different kinds of peeling.
